selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What strong qualities did the passage say he showed when he delivered the message and called people to the truth?
questions.answer: He showed steady commitment, firmness, and bravery.

questions.question: Which three character traits are highlighted first?
questions.answer: Steadiness, firmness, and courage.

questions.question: What does the passage show by saying he had no sign of panic or fear?
questions.answer: It shows he was completely brave and steady.

questions.question: What does that success show about him?
questions.answer: It shows that no one can equal him in delivering the message and inviting people to the truth.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the relationship between certainty and action?
questions.answer: It shows that deep certainty gives a person strength to keep going without wavering.

questions.question: Which believers are placed at the front of the saintly people in this passage?
questions.answer: The Companions are placed first among them.

questions.question: Which group is mentioned first as drawing from his belief and reaching high levels of faith?
questions.answer: The Companions are mentioned first.

questions.question: What role do the Companions play in this argument?
questions.answer: They are presented as leading examples of believers who drew from his faith.

questions.question: Which acts and qualities are gathered together before the final judgment?
questions.answer: His law, Islam, worship, supplication, call to truth, and faith are gathered together.

questions.question: What is the main idea of this passage?
questions.answer: It explains why his truthfulness is proven by his courage, his success in preaching, and the unmatched strength of his faith.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the amount of opposition he faced?
questions.answer: It says the opposition was very wide and very hostile.

questions.question: How serious was the resistance against him?
questions.answer: It was severe and came from major outside groups and from his own relatives and community.

questions.question: What can we infer from the fact that he showed no hesitation?
questions.answer: We can infer that he was completely sure of his mission.

questions.question: How is his faith described in terms of size and reach?
questions.answer: It is described as broad and world-illuminating.

questions.question: What groups of ideas were unable to weaken his belief?
questions.answer: The leading beliefs of the world, philosophical teachings, and religious teachings were unable to weaken it.

questions.question: According to the passage, who recognized him as the highest model of faith?
questions.answer: The saintly people across the ages, especially beginning with the Companions, recognized him that way.

questions.question: What did saintly believers of every age do in relation to his faith?
questions.answer: They took from it and accepted him as the greatest example of faith.

questions.question: Name two areas besides faith that are listed at the end as signs of his truthfulness.
questions.answer: His sacred law and his devotion in worship.

questions.question: What duty was he carrying out in this passage?
questions.answer: He was delivering Allah’s message and calling people to the truth.

questions.question: What did he keep doing even when many groups fought against him?
questions.answer: He kept calling people to the truth without backing down.

questions.question: What result is given as proof of his success in calling people to Islam?
questions.answer: He challenged the world and Islam became dominant in a major way.

questions.question: How does the passage use outcomes to support its point?
questions.answer: It points to his success in confronting the world and spreading Islam as evidence.

questions.question: What could not disturb his certainty, even with strong opposition?
questions.answer: The dominant beliefs of the age and the teachings of opposing thinkers could not disturb it.

questions.question: What effect did hostility and denial have on his inner confidence?
questions.answer: They did not create doubt, hesitation, weakness, or anxiety in him.
